data_basis: tradition_access_policies access levels and public governance scope
evidence_caveat: Public visibility never grants permission to collect restricted or initiatory knowledge.
Open and resolved-as-variants records remain visible; no forced single answer is produced.

data_basis: canonical entities, claims, evidence, conflicts and civilization membership
evidence_caveat: Coverage is a research-density indicator, never a completeness score or measure of cultural importance.

data_basis: claims assertion_scope, knowledge_layer, review_status and evidence evidence_type
evidence_caveat: Filters expose recorded labels; they do not upgrade uncertain evidence.
BASELINE_COMPLETE marks a bounded target checkpoint, not an all-complete tradition.
The timeline dates database releases; free-text mythic periods are not forced onto a modern absolute chronology.

data_basis: sources evidence_tier, verification_status, source_type and rights_status
evidence_caveat: Counts describe registered source metadata, not a universal ranking of traditions.

data_basis: stories, story_versions, story_sections, story_claim_links, story_entity_links and source metadata
evidence_caveat: Every section is an independent summary scoped to a named witness; gaps and variants remain visible.
notes: Initial cross-civilization reading release with 21 stories and 23 witness versions.

evidence_caveat: Release metadata comparison does not imply that historical coverage is complete.

data_basis: claims, evidence and sources connected to canonical entities
evidence_caveat: A graph edge means an explicit database link, not common origin or identity.

data_basis: place_profiles latitude/longitude joined to canonical entities
evidence_caveat: Only real places with explicit coordinates and a non-baseline evidence grade are plotted; missing coordinates are not inferred.
notes: The initial coordinate-backed layer is intentionally sparse.

data_basis: Build-time cards for every deity-classified entity: linked story versions, evidence-backed claim beats and access policies.
evidence_caveat: A card never adds facts: each beat is an existing claim with evidence, and permission-limited deities show their boundary instead of a story.
notes: Sealed: 184 deity cards — 111 linked to full stories, 71 evidence cards, 2 permission-limited.

evidence_caveat: Target failures and permission blocks remain visible and do not imply failure or completion for another tradition.
notes: The sealed checkpoint contains Maya, Japanese and Khmer stories; China and India remain queued, while Māori and Yorùbá are permission-gated.

data_basis: Generated from the same browser-safe story snapshot used by the public explorer.
evidence_caveat: The archive preserves source, locator, evidence-note and rights boundaries; it does not reproduce evidence short quotes.
notes: Sealed self-contained HTML and JSON remain searchable, bilingual and print-friendly while preserving source and rights boundaries.

data_basis: Versioned browser localStorage containing bookmarks, section progress and presentation settings only.
evidence_caveat: Local state is not evidence and never enters SQLite, JSONL, CSV or the public snapshot.
notes: Sealed on-device reader tools use a versioned localStorage key; no account, telemetry or cloud synchronization is introduced.

data_basis: All rows of story_expansion_batches with their targets, newest first.
evidence_caveat: Earlier sealed batches stay unchanged; a later batch can complete a target that an earlier batch recorded as queued.
notes: Sealed: the story library switches between the sealed v0.28 and v0.30 batch audits, newest first.

evidence_caveat: Alignment is editorial navigation. NOT_STATED and UNMODELED are explicit gaps, not negative claims.
notes: First batch covers Aphrodite origins and Ask/Embla creator triads.

data_basis: Full-screen, one-beat-at-a-time presentation of story sections and deity-card beats from the public snapshot.
evidence_caveat: Source notes and uncertainty notes stay one tap away on every beat.
notes: Keyboard, swipe and on-screen controls; preferences stay on the device.
